```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Bokor_2025_procalcitonin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Bokor_2025_procalcitonin"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10928-025-09965-8> (open access; the
  NM-TRAN control stream with the Scenario 0 final estimates and the
  per-scenario parameter tables are in Supplementary Material 1)

The paper is a methods study of how to impute missing within-day clock times
of birth and of blood sampling. The same turnover model was fitted to the
original data with all events at 00:00 of their date (Scenario 0) and to 100
replicate datasets for each of four imputation scenarios (1A, 1B, 2, 3).
Scenario 3, which follows the study hospital's sampling practice (first sample
of the day at 09:00, at least 8 h between samples), had the best objective
function (average dOFV -62.6 vs Scenario 0, Table 1) and the best VPC, so its
estimates are the model's typical values here.

# Population

The data are 1275 serum procalcitonin (PCT) concentrations from 282 Japanese
neonates and infants born at 22 to 41 weeks gestational age, measured during
routine care from birth up to 19 weeks postnatal age (Methods, first
paragraph; dataset of Fukuzumi 2016, Sci Rep 6:1-6). Sex, weight and the
number of preterm infants are not tabulated in the paper. The same information
is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Bokor_2025_procalcitonin")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `d/dt(central) <- kin * synb - cl * central / vc` | n/a | Eq. 1; Supplementary Text 1 `$DES` `DADT(2)` |
| `synb <- 1 + slope_birth * birth` | n/a | Eq. 2; `$DES` `SYNB` (VB = 1) |
| `central(0) <- kin / cl * vc` | n/a | Eq. 3; `$PK` `BASE`, `A_0(2)` |
| `fmat <- 1 / (1 + (PAGE / tm50_cl)^(-hill_cl))` | n/a | Eq. 4; `$PK` `FMAT` |
| `d/dt(birth) <- -kel_birth * birth`, `alag(birth) <- tlag` | n/a | Methods 'Modelling methods'; `$PK` `ALAG1`, `$DES` `DADT(1)` |
| `lkin` (RateInPCT) | 0.00466 ug/h | Table 2, Scenario 3 |
| `lcl` (CLPCT) | 0.493 L/h/70 kg | Table 2, Scenario 3 |
| `lvc` (VPCT) | 15 L/70 kg, fixed | Table 2; Methods (reference 17) |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | 0.75, 1, fixed | Methods 'Modelling methods'; `$PK` `PWRCL`, `VC` |
| `ltm50_cl` (TM50PCT) | 24.7 weeks | Table 2, Scenario 3 |
| `lhill_cl` (HillPCT) | 7.82 | Table 2, Scenario 3 |
| `lthalf_birth` (TelB) | 5.67 h | Table 2, Scenario 3 |
| `ltlag` (TLAG) | 12.0 h | Table 2, Scenario 3 |
| `lslope_birth` (SLOPEB) | 75.4 | Table 2, Scenario 3 |
| `etalkin` ... `etaltm50_cl` | `$OMEGA BLOCK(5)` | Supplementary Text 1 (Scenario 0) |
| `propSd` | 0.294 | Table 2, Scenario 3 |

# Model structure and units

The model runs in hours. Birth is a nominal bolus of 1 unit into the `birth`
compartment at the time of birth (time 0); `alag(birth)` holds it back for the
lag time, after which it decays with half-life TelB. PCT production is
`kin * (1 + slope_birth * birth)`, so before the lag production equals
baseline. PCT clearance and volume scale with weight to 70 kg and clearance
matures with postmenstrual age (`PAGE`, weeks).

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Bokor_2025_procalcitonin")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
```

# Typical-value time course (Figure 5 and Table 3)

Figure 5 and Table 3 simulate a male neonate of 40 weeks postmenstrual age and
3.36 kg at birth for four days. The control stream uses birth weight for the
first five days, so weight is held at 3.36 kg. Scenario 0 uses the control
stream's final estimates (converted from days to hours); the other scenarios
use the Table 2 averages over the 100 imputed datasets.

```{r scenarios}
scen <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario, ~kin, ~cl, ~tm50, ~hill, ~telb, ~tlag, ~slope,
  "0", 0.103 / 24, 10.5 / 24, 25.2, 11.7, 0.149 * 24, 0.826 * 24, 83.0,
  "1A", 0.00471, 0.500, 24.7, 7.80, 5.63, 15.3, 77.3,
  "1B", 0.00472, 0.502, 24.7, 7.85, 5.64, 15.6, 77.4,
  "2", 0.00471, 0.498, 24.6, 7.87, 5.70, 15.5, 77.9,
  "3", 0.00466, 0.493, 24.7, 7.82, 5.67, 12.0, 75.4
)

ev_ref <- rxode2::et(amt = 1, cmt = "birth", time = 0) |>
  rxode2::et(seq(0, 96, by = 0.05), cmt = "central")

solve_scenario <- function(row) {
  p <- c(
    lkin = log(row$kin), lcl = log(row$cl), ltm50_cl = log(row$tm50),
    lhill_cl = log(row$hill), lthalf_birth = log(row$telb),
    ltlag = log(row$tlag), lslope_birth = log(row$slope),
    WT = 3.36, PAGE = 40
  )
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_ref, params = p, atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10)
  data.frame(scenario = row$scenario, time = s$time, Cc = s$Cc, birth = s$birth)
}
typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(scen)), function(i) {
  solve_scenario(scen[i, ])
}))
```

```{r fig5, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 5 of Bokor 2025: typical PCT after birth for a 3.36 kg, 40-week PMA neonate under each scenario's estimates."}
ggplot(typ, aes(time / 24, Cc, colour = scenario, linetype = scenario)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after birth (days)", y = "Procalcitonin (ug/L)",
    colour = "Scenario", linetype = "Scenario"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The peak time and peak concentration are computed with PKNCA over 0 to 96 h
(the birth bolus is the nominal 1-unit dose).

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- typ |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L)
dose_df <- data.frame(id = 1L, scenario = scen$scenario, time = 0, amt = 1)
o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | scenario + id)
o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | scenario + id)
o_data <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  o_conc, o_dose,
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 96, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE)
)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(o_data)

table3 <- data.frame(
  scenario = c("0", "1A", "1B", "2", "3"),
  tmax = c(28.6, 26.9, 26.9, 23.5, 22.1),
  cmax = c(1.62, 2.09, 2.09, 2.07, 2.19)
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  nca, table3,
  by = "scenario",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/L", tmax = "h")
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs Table 3 of Bokor 2025.")
```

Scenario 0 is the only scenario whose printed parameters are the ones behind
the published curve, and it reproduces Table 3 to within about 2%. For
Scenarios 1A to 3, Table 3 and Figure 5 were drawn from the single replicate
whose dOFV was closest to the median, whose estimates are not printed; the
Table 2 averages used here are a different summary of the same 100 fits, so
differences of several percent are expected. The largest is the Scenario 2
peak time (about 26 h here vs 23.5 h). Its lag-time estimates spread from 12.7
to 21.2 h across the replicates (Supplementary Table 4), and the Figure 5 curve
for Scenario 2 starts rising at about 0.53 days (13 h), so the median-dOFV
replicate had a lag well below the 15.5 h average. The visible onset of the rise in
Figure 5 (about 0.47 days, 11 h, for Scenario 3; 0.8 days for Scenario 0) is
consistent with the lag times.

```{r check-table3}
nca_res <- as.data.frame(nca$result)
cell <- function(sc, code) {
  v <- nca_res$PPORRES[nca_res$scenario == sc & nca_res$PPTESTCD == code]
  if (length(v) != 1L) stop("no unique NCA row for scenario ", sc, " ", code)
  v
}
stopifnot(
  # Scenario 0: the printed control-stream estimates reproduce Table 3.
  abs(cell("0", "cmax") / 1.62 - 1) < 0.05,
  abs(cell("0", "tmax") - 28.6) < 1,
  # Scenario 3 (the selected model): average estimates against the
  # median-run Table 3 values.
  abs(cell("3", "cmax") / 2.19 - 1) < 0.15,
  abs(cell("3", "tmax") - 22.1) < 2,
  # Ordering reported in the Results: Scenario 3 peaks earliest and
  # Scenario 0 lowest.
  cell("3", "tmax") < cell("0", "tmax"),
  cell("0", "cmax") < min(sapply(c("1A", "1B", "2", "3"), cell, code = "cmax"))
)
```

# Baseline and closed-form checks

With weight and postmenstrual age held constant the model has an exact
solution. Before the lag the state stays at the baseline `kin / CL` (Eq. 3).
After the lag, with `tau = t - tlag`, `k = CL / V` and `kb = log(2) / TelB`,

`C(t) = base + kin * SLOPEB / V * (exp(-kb * tau) - exp(-k * tau)) / (k - kb)`.

The solver and the closed form share the same parameters, so the difference
is pure numerical error.

```{r closed-form}
p3 <- scen[scen$scenario == "3", ]
fsz <- 3.36 / 70
fmat <- 1 / (1 + (40 / p3$tm50)^(-p3$hill))
cl_i <- p3$cl * fsz^0.75 * fmat
v_i <- 15 * fsz
k <- cl_i / v_i
kb <- log(2) / p3$telb
base <- p3$kin / cl_i
s3 <- typ[typ$scenario == "3", ]
tau <- pmax(s3$time - p3$tlag, 0)
cf <- base + p3$kin * p3$slope / v_i * (exp(-kb * tau) - exp(-k * tau)) / (k - kb)
rel_err <- abs(s3$Cc - cf) / cf
c(baseline_ug_L = base, max_rel_err = max(rel_err))
stopifnot(
  max(abs(s3$Cc[s3$time < p3$tlag] / base - 1)) < 1e-6,
  max(rel_err) < 1e-4
)
```

# Maturation of PCT clearance

Equation 4 is a steep sigmoid in postmenstrual age. The Scenario 0 Hill
exponent (11.7) is close to a step change, which the authors judged
implausible; Scenario 3 gives a smoother curve (Hill 7.82).

```{r fmat, fig.cap = "Fraction of adult PCT clearance by postmenstrual age (Eq. 4) for Scenarios 0 and 3."}
pma <- seq(22, 60, by = 0.25)
fm <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(scenario = "0", PMA = pma, fmat = 1 / (1 + (pma / 25.2)^(-11.7))),
  data.frame(scenario = "3", PMA = pma, fmat = 1 / (1 + (pma / 24.7)^(-7.82)))
)
ggplot(fm, aes(PMA, fmat, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(x = "Postmenstrual age (weeks)", y = "Fmat (fraction of adult)") +
  theme_bw()
```

# Between-subject variability

A virtual cohort of 200 reference neonates (3.36 kg, 40 weeks PMA) shows the
spread the random effects imply over the first seven days. The variances are
those of the Scenario 0 fit (see Assumptions); the paper's Figure 4 VPCs pool
all ages and weights and cannot be reproduced without the individual data.

```{r vpc, fig.cap = "Simulated 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles of PCT (with residual error) for 200 reference neonates. Compare the shape with Figure 4 of Bokor 2025."}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20251)
n_sub <- 200L
ev_pop <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = seq_len(n_sub), time = 0, amt = 1, evid = 1L, cmt = "birth"),
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_len(n_sub), time = seq(0, 168, by = 2)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(WT = 3.36, PAGE = 40) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_pop)
sim_df <- as.data.frame(sim)
pct <- sim_df |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), p50 = median(sim), p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(pct, aes(time / 24)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p05), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(aes(y = p95), linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Postnatal day", y = "Procalcitonin (ug/L)") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r vpc-check}
ind_peak <- sim_df |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(cmax = max(Cc), .groups = "drop")
# The median individual peak sits near the typical-value peak; a
# mis-transcribed production rate, slope or volume moves it by far more.
c(median_cmax = median(ind_peak$cmax), typical_cmax = cell("3", "cmax"))
stopifnot(abs(median(ind_peak$cmax) / cell("3", "cmax") - 1) < 0.35)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Which estimates.** The typical values are the Scenario 3 averages over the
  100 imputed datasets (Table 2; Supplementary Table 5). The paper does not
  print the estimates of the median-dOFV replicate used for Figure 5 and
  Table 3.
* **Random effects carried from Scenario 0.** The paper reports variances only
  for Scenario 0 (the `$OMEGA BLOCK(5)` of the control stream). It states that
  the random-effects model was the same in every scenario, so those variances
  are used with the Scenario 3 typical values. They were estimated without
  clock-time imputation and probably overstate the spread, most clearly the
  SLOPEB variance (2.37). Use `rxode2::zeroRe()` for typical-value work. The
  variance on TelB was fixed to 0 in the control stream and is omitted.
* **Equation 1** is printed with `dC/dt` on the left and production and
  elimination rates on the right. The control stream integrates the PCT amount
  (`DADT(2) = RATEIN_PCT * SYNB - DCP * CL`), and that form is used here.
* **Weight.** The control stream uses birth weight for the first five days and
  the current weight, or an estimate from Sumpter and Holford 2011, after that.
  `WT` in this model is whatever weight the user supplies at each time; supply
  it on the same basis to reproduce the fit. The production rate is not
  weight-scaled, as in the control stream.
* **Volume scaling.** The volume is 15 L/70 kg, fixed from the calcitonin
  product label (paper reference 17), scaled linearly with weight.
* **Supplementary Table 4** (Scenario 2) lists SLOPEB as 75.4 with the same
  confidence interval as Scenario 3; main-text Table 2 gives 77.9 for
  Scenario 2. The vignette's Scenario 2 curve uses Table 2.
* **Units.** The control stream works in days (RATEIN 0.103 ug/day, CL
  10.5 L/day/70 kg, TELB 0.149 day, TLAG 0.826 day); Table 2 and this model
  use hours.
